text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- According to incomplete and unofficial local election returns the ruling Social Democratic Alliance (SDAM) has 53 municipalities, the opposition coalition 28, ethnic Albanian Party of Democratic Prosperity (PDP) 13, Socialist Party 7, and the opposition ethnic Albnaian Party of Democratic Prosperity of Albanians (PDP-A) four. Around 55 percent of Macedonian citizens voted.

- The opposition candidate Risto Penov was elected new Skopje mayor with 61,835 votes or 34.50 percent. Second came independent candidate Ljupco Nikolovski Fufo with 51,250 votes or 28.69 percent and third the SDAM candidate Jovica Ugrinovski with 25.40 percent.

- The ruling SDAM declared victory at the local elections in Macedonia. Secretary general Ljupco Popovski told a press conference that "SDAM is the party with the most votes in the country" and added he expected cooperation with opposition parties.

- The leading opposition coalition party, the Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation (IMRO) said the coalition won the cities in Macedonia, proving that "despite the SDAM's declaration of victory it is losing its position and becoming a rural party whose candidates were only elected in villages and small towns."
- The permanent OSCE mission in Skopje said the second round of local elections in Macedonia passed in a calm atmosphere. The only problem was absence of some citizens from electoral lists.
